headline_stat.name: Stouffer combined p, pre-stim choice decoding vs global trial-shuffle null (4 sessions)

stated_limitation: it is attenuated by the within-block shuffle control, which preserves block-level choice statistics; ... it is weak within unbiased P(left) = 0.5 blocks. About 10% of single units are individually choice-selective before stimulus onset (uncorrected p < 0.05 vs a 5% null expectation)

justification.dataset: IBL block-prior contrast-detection task (000149) is the canonical decision-bias paradigm and pre-stimulus choice decoding is a standard analysis for it.
justification.handling: Real data streamed via LINDI with explicit good-unit filtering, valid-trial selection, and premature-movement exclusion, all clearly justified.
justification.analysis: Logistic-regression decoding with repeated stratified CV, both global and within-block shuffle nulls, time-resolved decoding, and FWER-correct single-unit AUC nulls—the right methods done correctly.
justification.correctness: All headline numbers reproduce from the committed code and log and are internally consistent with the figures and CSV; only trivial imprecision in the stated accuracy range.
justification.figures: Figures show the effect clearly with units, sample sizes, and null bands, and the example units are the genuine top-AUC units including one at 0.42, not flattering picks.
justification.honesty: The write-up plainly reports that the within-block control removes significance and reinterprets the effect as a bias state, presents the single-unit effect as weak against its null band, and shows honest example units—calibrated to the evidence.
justification.verdict: Sound, thorough, and honestly hedged work that a supervisor would accept, with at most cosmetic fixes.
